# Toolkit Buildability Atlas — research agent for 100 apps

Take-home for Composio's AI Product Ops role. An agent researches 100 apps (auth, self-serve vs gated, API surface, MCP, buildability verdict) with evidence, verifies itself, and renders one self-explanatory HTML case study.

**Live page:** https://nikhilgaur1022.github.io/composio-app-research/
**Case study source:** `docs/index.html` (generated by `page/build.py`)

## What the agent does

```
apps.json ─▶ 1 registries ─▶ 2 probes ─▶ 3 pass 1 ─▶ 4 pass 2 ─▶ 5 judge ─▶ 6 merge ─▶ 7 human queue ─▶ site
              (no LLM)        (no LLM)    (Haiku,     (Sonnet,     (no LLM)   (vote +     (browser checks,
              Composio        401 probe,   snippets)   fetch docs,  quote      confidence,  corrections log)
              APIs.guru       OpenAPI/OIDC             quotes)      grounding) verdict)
              MCP registry    discovery
              GitHub
```

| Stage | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `agent/registries.py` | Composio toolkit catalog (SDK if `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is valid, else the public index), APIs.guru OpenAPI directory (exact endpoint count + security schemes), official MCP registry, GitHub search for MCP servers. |
| 2 | `agent/probes.py` | Empirical checks: fetch the hinted docs URL, hit the API base unauthenticated and read `WWW-Authenticate`/error body, look for `/openapi.json` and `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. |
| 3 | `agent/research.py` (pass 1) | Claude Code headless, Haiku, WebSearch only, no registry context. Deliberately weak baseline. |
| 4 | `agent/research.py` (pass 2) | Claude Code headless, Sonnet, WebSearch + WebFetch, registry/probe context injected, strict JSON schema, verbatim quotes required. |
| 5 | `agent/judge.py` | Fetches every cited URL and checks the quote actually appears on the page. Ungrounded evidence is discounted. |
| 6 | `agent/merge.py`, `agent/consistency.py` | Weighted vote per field across all sources → confidence = 0.4·agreement + 0.35·grounding + 0.25·self-report. Rule-based verdict. Vendor-family consistency checks. Low-confidence / conflicting rows go to `results/human_queue.json`. |
| 7 | `verification/` | `gold.json` (hand labels), `scoring.py` (accuracy per stage), `human_changes.json` (every human correction with evidence), `browser_checks.json` (Claude-in-Chrome checks with screenshots). |

## Run it

Requirements: Python 3.11+, a logged-in [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) CLI **or** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment (`claude -p` honors both). Optional: `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` in `.env` (without it the agent reads Composio's public catalog).

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m agent.run all --app "Attio"          # one app, all stages (~4 min)
python -m agent.run all                         # all 100, resumable, ~2h at default concurrency
python -m agent.run pass2 --retry-failed        # re-run only the LLM calls that failed
python -m verification.scoring                  # score pass1 / pass2 / merged / final vs gold
python -m page.build                            # regenerate docs/index.html
```

Every stage writes `results/<stage>/<app>.json`; existing outputs are skipped unless `--force`. Raw HTTP fetches are cached in `cache/` so judge and probes are free to re-run.

### Runnable trigger

`ci/research-one.workflow.yml` is a `workflow_dispatch` GitHub Action: enter an app name, it runs the whole pipeline for that app, rebuilds the page and commits. Copy it to `.github/workflows/` and add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as a repo secret to enable it (it lives in `ci/` because the token used to push this repo lacked the `workflow` scope). Locally the equivalent trigger is `python -m agent.run all --app "<name>" --force`.

## Where a human was needed

See the "Where a human was needed" and "Corrections log" sections on the page; the raw list is `verification/human_changes.json`. Short version: rebrands (fanbasis → Commas), bot-blocked sites (PitchBook), "apps" that are CLIs (Sherlock, Mermaid CLI), and the `access` field in general — docs rarely say "you need a paid plan"; pricing and signup pages do, and those need a browser.

## Honesty notes

- The Composio API key provided for this run returned 401, so the Composio SDK path could not be exercised live. The agent fell back to Composio's public toolkit index (`docs.composio.dev/toolkits.md`), which carries the same auth/tool-count data. The SDK path is implemented and is used automatically when a valid key is present.
- LLM calls ran through a Claude subscription via `claude -p`; costs on the page are the CLI's reported equivalents.
- Gold labels were produced by reading primary docs and pricing/signup pages; a few apps have "accepted alternative" labels where reasonable people would disagree (listed in `gold.json`).
